bull.b: Rising QCaaS revenue and a larger production-app mix indicate customers are moving beyond experimentation toward operational use. That supports a more repeatable services model, strengthens customer retention potential, and creates a foundation for recurring revenue growth as deployments expand.

The sharp increase in bookings and remaining performance obligations provides tangible evidence of commercial traction and improves forward revenue visibility. A growing contracted base can support scaling investments, deepen enterprise relationships, and reduce reliance on entirely new sales each quarter.

Peer-reviewed hardware validation combined with cloud-accessible simulator availability strengthens D-Wave’s dual-platform strategy. This can help attract developers and enterprise partners while building an ecosystem around both current annealing applications and longer-term fault-tolerant computing.

bear.b: Operating losses are expanding while the company invests heavily in development and go-to-market efforts, showing that commercial growth has not yet produced operating leverage. Persistent losses could constrain strategic flexibility and make successful execution of the roadmap increasingly important.

bear.t: Persistent cash burn and reduced liquidity
bear.b: Continued negative operating and free cash flow means D-Wave is consuming capital to fund operations rather than self-financing growth. The lower cash balance reduces liquidity headroom, while ongoing investment and losses may increase reliance on additional external funding over time.

Concentrating expected revenue in a small number of system deliveries creates timing risk and makes reported growth uneven between periods. This volatility can complicate planning, obscure underlying recurring demand, and leave results dependent on successful shipment and installation execution.
